title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 136 (Surety not discharged when agreement made with third person to give time to principal debtor)

content.overview: Section 136 provides that where a contract to give time to the principal debtor is made by the creditor with a third person, and not with the principal debtor, the surety is not discharged. The statutory illustration confirms that a contract with a third person concerning an overdue bill does not discharge the surety.
content.glance: A contract to give time made with a third person (not the principal debtor) does not discharge the surety.
content.study: Where a contract to give time to the principal debtor is made by the creditor with a third person, and not with the principal debtor, the surety is not discharged. Illustration: C, the holder of an overdue bill of exchange drawn by A as surety for B, and accepted by B, contracts with M to give time to B. A is not discharged. Current-law framing: distinguish from Section 135 (contract with the principal debtor itself); the third-person route does not discharge.

examples.title: Time given via third person
examples.body: Creditor contracts with a third person to give the principal debtor more time. Under Section 136 the surety is not discharged.

hypotheticals.question: The creditor agrees with a friend of the principal debtor to allow extra time, without contracting with the principal debtor. Is the surety discharged?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 136 provides that a contract to give time made with a third person (not the principal debtor) does not discharge the surety.
